source: Own measurement through `ale validate`: run validate-bc3c4ffd on the tree of c32222a7, the pinned engine bfb7505 (0.1.1), the privileged reference (solution/solve.sh, token truth) as the oracle episode, graded in the engine's separate verifier sandbox (the cell as its own account from a private copy, the seccomp launcher, the kit's Solver and probe lock, one fresh cell process per row section) on the fixed hidden set (tests/hidden/rows.json, six row sections): mean_row_yield 1.00000, every row 1.0 (4, 4, 4, 6, 4 and 5 of their ready trusses delivered, 27 of 27) in 218, 241, 270, 356, 251 and 300 steps, 214 to 328 s simulated (the allowance is 430 s); no protective stop, no truss damaged, no leaf cut, nothing cut that was not ready; the probe lock 39 of 40 (5 idle pairs not counted); the verify stage 435 s; the untouched sandbox 0.0. Its distance from each cliff: a cut peduncle at most 0.11 mm off the mouth's mid-plane (the mouth takes about 5 mm) and 0.35 mm off its centre along the tool axis (7 mm), the closing force 1.15 times a peduncle's cutting force (crushed above 1.4), the largest change of a fruit's velocity in a control tick 0.86 m/s (bruised above 1.5), the largest press on a fruit 8.9 N (bruised above 25). Host: the author's validate host, one NVIDIA RTX 3090 on driver 535.183.01 (below Omniverse RTX's R550 floor, hence the cell's driver check off; the canary passed), an Intel i9-12900K, Docker 29.10.1 in rootless mode, which cannot set a CPU quota: the engine's --cpus 8 was dropped and every process started through docker exec was pinned to 8 CPUs by affinity (OCI execCPUAffinity) instead; memory and the GPU as the engine requested. The same value in the same steps as the two native runs of tests/verify.py as an ordinary account on that host (on the trees of 43aaafc9 and 82577516; tests/README.md, section 6).
note: mean_row_yield is the mean over the hidden row sections of (ready trusses that count) / (ready trusses of the row) (rowcell/rules.py `credit`), already on [0, 1]; the reference delivers every ready truss, so the value is 1 by construction and any honest run of it reads 1.0 unless a truss is lost. ratio = measured / value, reward = clamp(ratio / full_at, 0, 1). full_at 0.9: on the author's machine the reference repeats each row step for step; what a contact-rich run on another CPU can lose is a truss here and there (a truss that settles on a neighbour, a harder landing), and one truss of the 27 moves mean_row_yield by 0.028 to 0.042 (a sixth or a quarter of one row's sixth): 0.9 leaves room for two. On fourteen review rows of the same cultivar outside the set (71 ready trusses) the reference delivered all but two before its last change (two trusses pressed onto a crate's floor with 27 and 31 N) and every truss of the four rows re-run after it, those two rows among them (tests/README.md, section 6). It has to be sized again from `ale validate` runs on the evaluation hosts.
